newsitem.title: USA: Clinton expresses concern for Yeltsin health.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expresses concern for Yeltsin health.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was concerned by reports that Russian President Boris Yeltsin will undergo heart surgery, and the U.S. embassy in Moscow was seeking further details, a White House spokesman said on Thursday.

"The president is obviously concerned to hear about President Yeltsin's health," White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry told reporters on Air Force One shortly before landing in Florida, where Clinton is to begin a two-day campaign swing.
"We don't have any official information from our embassy yet," he said.
McCurry said Clinton "certainly wishes him all the best for a full and speedy recovery."
In Moscow, the RIA news agency said Yeltsin had agreed to have a heart operation, likely at the end of September in Moscow.
Yeltsin, who had two heart attacks last year, disappeared from public view on June 26. Aides denied he was ill, saying only that the president was exhausted after a gruelling election campaign.
